reports.msg: Containment has increased to 50%. A total of 467 firefighters remain assigned, working to strengthen containment lines and extinguish hot spots, per OCFA on X.

Size: 570 acres

Containment: 25%

Crews will work to increase containment and begin suppression repair — repairing areas disturbed by firefighting to help reduce erosion.

Update from Orange County Fire Authority on X

All evacuation orders have been lifted, per Orange County Sheriff's Department.

The latest release includes evacuation zones SCL12, SJC04, SJC05, and the remaining portion of SJC10 (SJC 10 A). Previously released areas include all of SCL13 and part of SJC10 (SJC 10 B).

Via La Mirada will remain closed, north of Esperanza to vehicle traffic, to allow OCFA emergency vehicles to continue work. The burn scar is an active fire hazard area and is closed until further notice. Reference the map at this link for the closure area.

With these changes, no Evacuation Orders associated with the Norte Fire remain in effect. Residents may return, subject to any remaining road closures or access restrictions.

Please use caution when returning to the area. Emergency personnel may continue operating nearby, and certain roads or locations may remain restricted. Follow directions from public safety personnel.

The fire is currently at 25% containment, per Orange County Fire Authority on X.

The evacuation order has been lifted for Zones SCL13 and SJC 10 B.

Zone SJC 10 has been split:

  • Evacuations have been lifted for Zone SJC 10 B. This area is limited to the Stallion Ridge community, San Juan Hills High School, and the landfill off La Pata.

  • Zone SJC 10 A remains under an Evacuation Order.

Per the Orange County Evacuation Map. These changes are also visible on the Watch Duty Map.

Please use caution when returning to the area. Emergency personnel may continue operating nearby, and certain roads or locations may remain restricted. Follow directions from public safety personnel. Per Orange County Sheriff's Department.
Zone SCL13 remains under an Evacuation Order, per the Orange County Evacuation Map. The previously reported status change was done in error. Evacuation zones can also be viewed on the Watch Duty map.

The Evacuation Order has been lifted for Zone SCL13, per the Orange County Evacuation Map. This change is also visible on the Watch Duty Map.

Correction: Zone SCL13 remains under an Evacuation Order, per the Orange County Evacuation Map. The previously reported status change was done in error. Evacuation zones can also be viewed on the Watch Duty map.

The fire is 5% contained and remains at 570 acres. Crews worked throughout the night to attack the fire and strengthen containment lines. Today, crews will continue working to increase containment and get residents back home as soon as it is safe to do so. Per OCFA on X.

All evacuation orders remain in effect. Crews will continue working throughout the night to protect homes and keep communities safe.

A video update provided by OCFA on X can be seen above.

An overnight shelter is open at the Boys & Girls Club located at 1 Via Positiva, San Juan Capistrano. Animals will be allowed. Bring your medications if possible.

Animal Shelters

For San Juan Capistrano Residents:

For residents of San Juan Capistrano under mandatory evacuation orders, OC Animal Care established an emergency animal shelter to provide services for residents relocated as a result of the Norte Fire. This shelter is open to house dogs, cats, and small pets.

The OC Animal Care shelter is located at 1630 Victory Road, Tustin.

If possible, pet owners should bring photo identification, veterinary/vaccination records, special food, and medications along with their animals.

Any person needing assistance with information about pets or large animal evacuations should call OC Animal Care at 714-935-6848 from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. or 714-259-1122 from 5 p.m. to 8 a.m.

For San Clemente Residents:

For residents of San Clemente, the San Clemente/Dana Point Animal Shelter (CASA) is accepting pets from San Juan Capistrano and San Clemente evacuees. The shelter will remain open for accepting animals until 7 PM and will reopen at 7 AM.

The CASA shelter is located at 221 Avenida Fabricante, San Clemente.

Care & Reception

Care and reception are available from 8:00 AM - 8:00 PM at:

  • San Juan Capistrano Community Center at 25925 Camino del Avion, San Juan Capistrano

  • San Clemente Community Center at 100 Calle Seville, San Clemente

Per Orange County Sheriff's Department.

The fire has been mapped at 570.3 acres by FIRIS OES Intel 24. Their perimeter is visible on the Watch Duty map under the Active Fire Perimeters map layer.

Note: Fire perimeters are preliminary and indicate general burn area but do not reflect structure protection efforts by firefighters. A structure within a fire perimeter may not be damaged or destroyed.

The fire is currently 0% contained. The objective is to keep the fire within its current perimeter and prevent it from growing. 400 personnel are assigned, with an additional 400 personnel responding. Resources will be out all night, tomorrow, and into the weekend.

The following shelters remain open and small pets are accepted:

  • San Clemente Community Center: 100 N Calle Seville, San Clemente

  • San Juan Capistrano Community Center: 25925 Camino Del Avion, San Juan Capistrano

Officials are continually evaluating repopulation, but it will not occur until it's deemed safe. A public information hotline remains available at 714-628-7085.

View the full recording of the Norte Fire Press Conference on the Orange County Fire Authority Facebook page.
Six air tankers have been released and the no-divert status has been lifted, per Air Attack.

The fire has been mapped at 465.5 acres by FIRIS OES Intel 24. Their perimeter is visible on the Watch Duty map under the Active Fire Perimeters map layer.

Note: Fire perimeters are preliminary and indicate general burn area but do not reflect structure protection efforts by firefighters. A structure within a fire perimeter may not be damaged or destroyed.

Nine Capistrano Unified School District schools are dismissing students early Friday, Oct. 16, as the Norte Fire prompts evacuations near San Clemente and San Juan Capistrano.

The affected schools are:

  • Bernice Ayer Middle School

  • Clarence Lobo Elementary School

  • Concordia Elementary School

  • Harold Ambuehl Elementary School

  • San Clemente High School

  • San Juan Hills High School

  • Shorecliffs Middle School

  • Truman Benedict Elementary School

  • Vista Del Mar

Parents and guardians of elementary school students are being asked to report directly to their schools for pickup. At secondary schools, families may pick up students or authorize their release by responding to school communications.

Families should continue monitoring messages from Capistrano Unified and follow official evacuation instructions from public safety agencies.

Update via Orange County Department of Education on Facebook.

Evacuation shelters are available at the following locations:

  • San Juan Capistrano Community Center 25925 Camino del Avion, San Juan Capistrano.

  • San Clemente Community Center 100 Calle Seville, San Clemente.

Update via OCFA on X.

Units have been requested to the area of La Novia and Via Cerro Rebal for an immediate structure threat.

An additional resource request has been placed for 50 type-1 engines, 15 type-3 wildland engines, 3 hand crews, and 6 dozers. A road closure has been requested for Avenida La Pata, southbound between Ortega Hwy and Avenida Vista Hermosa, per radio traffic.
A hard road closure has been requested from I-5 at San Juan Creek Rd to Camino De Los Mares, per radio traffic.

An Evacuation Order is in place for Zones SJC04, SJC05, SJC 10, SCL12, and SCL13, per the Orange County Evacuation Map. These zones are also visible on the Watch Duty map.

The fire is now 250 acres, per OC Fire Authority on X.

An Evacuation of all streets off Camino Las Ramblas down to I-5 and around to the San Juan dump has been requested. The fire is impacting homes in the area of Avenida Calita, Via La Mirada, and Via De Agua in San Juan Capistrano. Per radio traffic.

Multiple structures are impacted in the area of Via La Mirada and Calle Esperanza. Additionally units are responding to reported structure threats in the area of Avenida California and Paseo Aliso. 10 additional type-1 strike teams (50 engines) have been requested, per radio traffic.
